requirements.requirement: Files, directories, paths, environment access and cleanup
requirements.details: 32 typed signatures provide strict UTF-8 and binary reads/writes, exclusive creation/copy, append, native rename, exact wide byte sizes, existence/kind inspection, sorted directory names, recursive/empty cleanup, explicit temporary directories, native lexical/canonical paths and immutable environment snapshots. No cwd or environment globals are changed.

requirements.requirement: Explicit mutation and symlink behavior with ordinary diagnostics
requirements.details: Inputs are checked before writes; Create and Copy atomically reject existing destinations, including dangling links; ordinary filesystem errors preserve call/source context and previous destinations. Entry operations normalize trailing separators/dots before no-follow lookup/removal. Recursive cleanup leaves symlink targets intact. Root/parent rejection is exercised through a pure validator; real deletion tests use owned temporary directories. Unix temporary creation requests mode 0700.

requirements.requirement: Admission before payload copying or mutation
requirements.details: Return admission precedes mutation; opened file length is preflighted, growth is incrementally admitted and shrinking files release unused credit. Directory entries and environment data retain normal values/temporary limits. Path construction has a checked 1 MiB workspace bound. Allocator observations prove rejected metadata skips large file buffers and rejected environment results skip their payload copy.

requirements.requirement: Async isolation, run configuration and cooperative stop handling
requirements.details: Filesystem calls use the existing bounded native pool; pure path/environment helpers stay inline. Engine environments share owners, while standalone Context directory copies are charged before handoff. A real Linux FIFO with a finite watchdog proves single-thread executor progress. Read/write loops handle interruption, short writes, stop checks and incomplete effects. Concurrent runs retain separate directories/environment snapshots.

requirements.requirement: Platform reference, metadata, examples and conformance
requirements.details: The fixed catalogue has 89 slots. Registration remains idempotent and preserves host overrides; snapshot/completion/CLI checks reflect the expanded catalogue. The reference and example 32 execute a temporary-directory file workflow with Finally cleanup. B5 corpus cases cover success, empty paths/components and typed input/I/O failures. Native platform differences, partial effects, permissions, no sandbox, and non-preemptible syscalls are documented.

review_notes: A manual audit in an owned temporary fixture reproduced the standard-library trailing-slash symlink behavior: target contents were visited before removal failed. Entry operations now strip redundant trailing separators/dots through native components, without collapsing parent components or canonicalizing symlinks. Four suffix regression cases verify target preservation.

Root/terminal-parent removal validation was extracted into a pure helper. Its negative tests perform no filesystem calls, including when mutation testing deliberately breaks the validator. Destructive integration probes operate only within independently owned temporary fixtures.

Standalone worker contexts previously used an empty directory because ordinary host callbacks needed only the immutable run environment. Only filesystem built-ins now request an admitted standalone directory copy; existing callbacks and Engine environment sharing retain their behavior.

Streaming temporary reservations add payload/nodes without adding a value handle. Growth checks are transactional and shrinking length hints release unused credit; rejected growth cannot silently bypass live limits.

The previous regex worker mutation anchor was narrowed to its unchanged regex predicate because the same method now also dispatches filesystem workers. Its semantic fault is unchanged; the earlier 121 catalogue entries remain represented alongside 22 OS faults.

Initial path testing exposed a trailing separator for Absolute Path with an empty input. The implementation now returns the directory snapshot exactly. Existing completion expectations were updated for the added Read/Remove names.
A broad draft catalogue-count documentation edit also touched duration-boundary digits; review restored those unchanged numeric boundaries before the frozen matrix. No date/time semantics changed.

Production default limits were not raised. Existing fixed-table snapshot expectations were updated from 57 to 89 slots, while the table capacity remained within the existing allocation oracle threshold.
limits: This 32-statement contract does not claim complete Robot Framework OperatingSystem API compatibility.
Paths follow native filesystem rules and the executing identity permissions. Absolute/parent paths and intermediate symlinks remain allowed; this is not an isolation or containment boundary.

Individual syscalls and recursive standard-library operations cannot be forcibly interrupted. Cancellation observes checkpoints and drains started workers; completed or partial effects are not rolled back.
Temporary directories persist after successful creation and require explicit cleanup. There is no automatic end-of-run or abandoned-result cleanup guarantee.
File output uses value/temporary limits; streaming Copy has no separate total disk-byte quota. Logical path workspace is bounded separately from library-owned OS buffers and allocator overhead.

Copy creates a new destination and does not preserve source metadata. Rename uses native replacement rules and has no cross-filesystem copy fallback. Writes do not promise fsync durability or concurrent append record atomicity.
Environment access reads immutable configured snapshots, requires an Engine environment and rejects non-UTF-8 returned data. It adds neither global mutation nor case folding.

The initial musl debug run observed EAGAIN in existing worker-tree startup coverage; the exact test and repeated full run passed unchanged. The intermittent cause remains unconfirmed and is retained as follow-up work.

Linux GNU and musl are validated. Windows/macOS descriptions follow library contracts without claiming platform test runs. No new coverage percentage, complete generated mutation score, or performance guarantee is claimed.

focused=['--test','setup_failure','--test','suite_fixtures','--test','documentation','--test','examples','--test','conformance']
commands=[('gnu-debug-full',['cargo','test','--locked']),('gnu-release-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--release']),('musl-debug-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--target','x86_64-unknown-linux-musl']),('musl-release-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--release','--target','x86_64-unknown-linux-musl']),('clippy-gnu',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('clippy-musl',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--target','x86_64-unknown-linux-musl','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('format',['cargo','fmt','--all','--','--check']),('coverage-helper',['python3','tests/coverage_tools.py']),('mutation-helper',['python3','tests/mutation_tools.py'])]

try:
 for label,command in commands:
  print('running '+label,flush=True)
  log=out/(label+'.log')
  with log.open('w') as stream:
   result=subprocess.run(command,stdout=stream,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=1200,env=dict(os.environ,CARGO_BUILD_JOBS='2'))
  content=log.read_text()
  rows=re.findall(r'test result: (?:ok|FAILED)\. (\d+) passed; (\d+) failed; (\d+) ignored;',content)
  check={'label':label,'command':command,'status':result.returncode,'log':str(log.relative_to(root)),'tests':dict(zip(('passed','failed','ignored'),[sum(int(row[i]) for row in rows) for i in range(3)]))}
  record['checks'].append(check)
  (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2)+'\n')
  print(json.dumps(check),flush=True)
  if result.returncode:
   print(content[-12000:],flush=True)
   raise SystemExit(result.returncode)
 record['complete']=True
finally:
 record['finished']=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
 (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2)+'\n')
